credit: Scott Olson/Getty Images via Hollywood Reporter
story: Kalshi launched a prediction market with $3M in trading volume betting on which song would be Spotify's most-streamed in June 2026; a trader then bought over 500,000 fake streams to push obscure artist Malcolm Todd's 'Earrings' to #1, collected the payout — and Spotify only removed the fraudulent streams after the market had already been settled and winners paid, exposing the fundamental design flaw in building a financial instrument on a metric any bettor can directly manipulate.
why_funny: Kalshi spent months engineering a sophisticated prediction market on Spotify's chart data and apparently never considered that anyone with enough skin in the game could simply purchase a #1 for a fraction of the payout.
